spec_match.rationale: The page now uses the current named-trigger CSS syntax and labels its Web Animations interaction as an illustration, but it does not execute the native timeline-trigger no-auto-rewind sequence.

interactive.rationale: Repeated play and reset controls produce observable animation and state changes.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index blurb now describes the actual syntax check and labelled illustration instead of promising an absent configuration tool.

edge_cases.rationale: Finished and reset states are shown, but play-forwards, play-backwards, direction reversal, and native trigger re-entry remain uncovered.

references.rationale: The canonical ChromeStatus feature and CSSWG specification are directly linked.

conformance.rationale: The visible inherited suite exposes one incorrect legacy assertion using animation-trigger: view(); the current grammar requires a dashed trigger name and the behavior change itself is not asserted.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chrome DevTools MCP at 390×844 and 1280×800 exercised play, finished re-play, and reset; exact widths held and console/network were clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: Shared telemetry records interactions, but the page does not yet emit a dedicated assertion for the native Chrome 151 behavior.

design_system.rationale: The focused repair uses shared variables, responsive layout, and the shared visible test panel.

accessibility.rationale: Native named buttons retain visible focus and changing support/readout text is exposed as polite status content.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Both tested viewports are usable with no document overflow; the complete conformance list remains visible on both.

openQuestions.title: Build the native timeline re-entry proof
openQuestions.detail: Use the WPT structure: a named timeline-trigger source, animation-trigger: --trigger play/play-forwards/play-backwards, scroll entry/exit/re-entry, and direct currentTime/playState/playbackRate evidence. Keep this illustration route unchanged and add the native proof as a new route.

openQuestions.title: Add an action configuration matrix
openQuestions.detail: Provide a tool covering play, play-once, play-forwards, play-backwards, pause, reset, and replay across initial/running/paused/finished states, using the specification table as the source.

guidanceConsulted.query: Expose live feature detection and conformance test results as an accessible educational details interface
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic structure, native controls, concise status announcements, visible focus, and source-linked alternatives for visual state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied native buttons and polite status regions; the shared panel renders a labelled section with every result visible rather than hiding headings inside a disclosure.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Chrome DevTools MCP accessibility snapshot showed named buttons, status regions, one document H1, and a labelled What this browser supports region.

summary: Corrected fabricated browser-age messaging and invalid view() syntax. The page is now an honest, responsive illustration with visible checks, but native runtime and full action-portfolio demos remain required.
